 Judgment
Challenging the award in MVC No.543/2015 on the file of the Prl.MACT and SCCH-1 Bengaluru, the claimant in the said case has preferred this appeal.

2. On 18.10.2014 at 8.30 p.m. when the claimant was traveling with her father on motor cycle bearing No.KA-04/EL 8111 near BB road within the limits of Yelahanka Police Station, tanker lorry bearing No.KA-10/7943 hit the motor cycle and caused the accident.
Consequently, the claimant suffered grievous injuries.
Initially she was treated in Apoorva Hospital and from there she was shifted to Columbia Asia Hospital.
From there she was shifted to Ramaiah hospital.
Due to the injuries suffered by her, her left leg was amputated.

At the relevant time, respondent No.2 was the registered NC: 2023:KHC:21401-DB owner, respondent No.3 was the subsequent purchaser of the said vehicle and respondent No.1 was the Insurer of the said vehicle.

3. The claimant filed MVC No.543/2015 against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- on the ground that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence of the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-10/7943.
She further contended that due to the injuries suffered in the accident she has suffered permanent physical disability.
Therefore, the respondents are liable to compensate the same.

4. Respondents No.1 and 2 contested the petition denying the occurrence of the accident, actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry, the injuries suffered by the claimant, her age and their liability to pay the compensation.
The first respondent further contended that at the time of the accident the lorry had no valid permit.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation.
5. On behalf of the claimant PWs.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.P1 to P18 were marked.
Respondent Nos.2 and 3 did not lead any evidence.

On behalf of the first NC: 2023:KHC:21401-DB N. Swathi vs The Manager on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199510070/
2 respondent RWs.1 to 3 were examined and Exs.R.1 to R10 were marked.
6.
The Tribunal on hearing the parties by the impugned award held that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the tanker lorry.
The Tribunal relying on the medical evidence assessed the disability of the claimant at 80%.

The Tribunal considered the income of the claimant notionally at Rs.6,000/-, added 50% of the same by way of future prospects, applied 18 multiplier and awarded compensation of Rs.15,55,200/- by way of loss of future earnings.
7. The Tribunal in all awarded Rs.22,49,800/- on different heads as per the table below.

Pain and Sufferings 60,000/-
 2. Medical expenses 29,600/-
 3. Food and Nourishment, 40,000/-
 conveyance attendant charges  and other incidental expenses  4. Loss of future earning due to 15,55,200/-

For purchase of artificial limb 3,00,000/-

 10. Change of Socket throughout 40,000/-
 her life
The Tribunal further held that as on date of the accident there was no permit for operating the vehicle.
Therefore, Insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.
Thus fastened the liability to respondent No.2 the registered owner/Policy holder.
9. Challenging the adequacy of the compensation and the finding that respondent no.2 shall pay the compensation, the claimant has preferred the above appeal.

10. Smt.Kalpana P.V., learned counsel for the appellant submits that the compensation awarded for future medical expenses, the notional income of the victim considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The compensation awarded on the other heads is on the lower side.

11. Relying on the judgment of Supreme Court in Amrit Paul Singh and another vs. Tata AIG General Insurance NC: 2023:KHC:21401-DB Company Ltd. she submits that Tribunal should have directed the Insurer to pay the compensation and recover the same from the insured - registered owner of the vehicle.

entities.text: Amrit Paul Singh and another vs. Tata AIG General Insurance NC: 2023:KHC:21401-DB Company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Per contra, Sri Janardhana Reddy, learned counsel for the Insurer submits that compensation awarded on all the heads is just and reasonable one.

He further submits that at the time of accident,
vehicle had no permit to operate, therefore, the insurer was justifiably exonerated.
Therefore, that finding also does not warrant interference.
ANALYSIS 13.
None of the respondents have preferred any appeal challenging the finding of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of lorry KA-10/7943.
Therefore, that finding has attained finality.

Reg. Quantum:
14.
As per the evidence of PW.2, due to injuries suffered in the accident, left leg of the claimant was amputated above knee.
PW.2 the Doctor who treated her and conducted (2018) 7 SCC 558.

NC: 2023:KHC:21401-DB surgery for amputation assessed her permanent physical disability at 80%
to the whole body.
That finding is not under challenge.
15. The victim, at the time of the accident was a student, aged 17 years and she was capable of earning.
As per Ex.P10 the certificate issued by Narayana PU College, the claimant was studying in I Year PUC.

The Tribunal states that Rs.7,000/- is reasonable notional income, but, subsequently,
considered the same as Rs.6,000/-.

Considering the age of the claimant, cost of living, prevailing wage rates during the relevant period, it is just and appropriate to consider the notional income of the claimant at Rs.8,500/- per month.

16. Since the claimant had no permanent employment, as per the Judgment of the Supreme Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi2, the Tribunal should have assessed the future prospects at 40% of her income and not at 50%.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicable multiplier is `18'.
Therefore, 80% of Rs. 8500/- comes to Rs.6,800/-, 40% of 6800/- comes to Rs. 2,720/-.

Therefore, the total monthly income of the victim 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) NC: 2023:KHC:21401-DB comes to (6,800+2720) =
Rs.9,520/-.

Therefore, loss of future earnings comes to (Rs.9,520/- x 12 x 18) = Rs. 20,56,320/-.
17.
The claimant was hospitalized for 49 days.
She underwent amputation of left lower limb.

Considering her age, period of hospitalization and trauma, the compensation of Rs.60,000/-

4 awarded on the head of `Pain and Suffering' is on the lower side.

sentences.text: Thus, it is just and proper to enhance it to Rs.1,00,000/-.
18. The compensation towards `Medical Expenses' was based on the documents produced.
That does not warrant interference.

Similarly, compensation awarded under the head `food,
transportation, and attendant charges' as awarded by the Tribunal is just one.

19. Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant, period of hospitalization and deprivation of claimant from enjoyment of her routine privileges like a normal person of her age,
award of Rs.50,000/- by the Tribunal towards `Loss of amenities in life' is on the lower side.
It is just and proper to enhance the same to Rs.1,00,000/-.
Further, the compensation awarded on the head of `loss of marriage prospects' at Rs.75,000/- is on the lower side.
Having regard to the nature of injuries i.e., amputation of leg suffered by her, her marriage prospects become bleak.
It is submitted that the claimant is aged 23 years and not yet married.
Under such circumstances, awarding of Rs.2,00,000/- under the head of `Loss of Marriage Prospects' meets the ends of justice.
21. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- on the head of `loss of earnings' of the father of the claimant during the laid up period.
Admittedly the claimant's father who was her next friend before the Tribunal was a Railway employee.
The Tribunal held that he had availed leave for a period of two months thereby, he loses leave encashment.
However, no evidence was lead to show that he lost the leave encashment during the said period.
Therefore, the Tribunal was not justified in presuming that he lost leave encashment and awarding Rs.50,000/- under the loss of income of the father during the period of treatment of the petitioner.
For purchase of artificial limb, Tribunal has awarded Rs.3,00,000/-.
Nothing was produced before the Tribunal to show that the claimant had purchased the artificial limb.
Ex . P.9
which was produced to justify the purchase is just an estimation letter and not a receipt for having paid the money.

23. Smt.Kalpana P.V., learned counsel appearing for the claimant, on instructions fairly submitted that, the artificial limb was purchased by the employer of the claimant's father and he has not incurred any expenses on the same.

Though the claimant did not lead any evidence regarding her future surgery, PW.2 the Doctor who treated her deposed that she has to undergo one more surgery to correct the protruded bone/revision amputation surgery and according to him, she needs Rs.75,000/- to 1,00,000/- for the said correction.

The learned counsel for the appellant relying on the judgment of Supreme Court in Mohd.Saber @ Shabir Hussain vs. Regional Manager, U.P.State Road Transport Corporation3 submitted that the compensation awarded for the change of socket of the artificial limb is on the lower side.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering Civil Appeal Nos.9070-9071/2022 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:21401-DB the evidence of PW.2 and the judgment of the Supreme Court in the above referred case, this Court is of the opinion that awarding global compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- on the head of `future surgery and maintenance of artificial limb', meets the ends of justice.

25. For the aforesaid reasons, the just compensation payable is as follows:

 2. Medical expenses 29,600/-
 3. Food and Nourishment, 40,000/-
 conveyance attendant charges  and other incidental expenses  4. Loss of future earning due to 20,56,320/-
 permanent disability  5. Loss of amenities 1,00,000/-
 6. Loss of marriage prospects 2,00,000/-
 7. Future surgery and 3,00,000/-
 maintenance of socket  throughout her life

Total 28,25,920/-
 Rounded off to  Rs.28,26,000/-

Reg. Liability:
26.
The evidence of RW Nos.2 and 3 and Exs. R1 to 10 show that at the time of the accident the vehicle had no permit - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:21401-DB at all to operate.
Therefore, the Tribunal has fastened the liability to respondent No.2 who was the insured as well as the registered owner of the vehicle at the time of the accident.
Respondent No.2 has not challenged the said finding.

However, as per the judgment of the Supreme Court in Amrith Paul Singh's case referred to supra, even in case of operating of the vehicle without permit, the insurer has to reimburse the compensation amount and recover the same from N. Swathi vs The Manager on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199510070/
6 insured/registered owner.
Therefore, the award with regard to liability requires to be modified accordingly.
27. For the aforesaid reasons, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.

ii) The impugned award is modified as follows:
(a) The claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.28,26,000/- with interest thereon at 6% p.a.from the date of petition till its realization.
(b) Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the said compensation.
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:21401-DB c) The 1st respondent/Insurer shall deposit the said amount on adjusting the amount already deposited if any, before the Tribunal within four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and shall recover the same form respondent No.2.
Respondent No.1 has the right to seek attachment and sale of offending lorry for recovery of the amount.
d) On such deposit, the Tribunal shall release the same digitally to the claimant on furnishing the required documents.
e) Registry shall transmit the TCRs to the Tribunal forthwith.
